issue_text: In shardResultBlockers, a result is matched to a shard by its content hash (MatchShard), giving id = "shard-"+shard.ID. The guard at lines 419-422 (`if strings.TrimSpace(result.ShardID) != id`) is the ONLY check that the result's self-declared ShardID field actually equals the shard its hash belongs to. It is deletable with every test still passing: no test asserts the blocker it emits ("... declares shard ..."). Grep confirms the literal "declares shard" appears only in manifest.go, never in a test.
why_real: Category 2 (invariant nothing holds). Exploit: a result with ShardHash = the hash of shard-3a, ShardID = "shard-b1", and Path = ".../shard-b1.<hash>.result.json". MatchShard resolves it to shard-3a (id="shard-3a"); the filename check at 482-489 uses want=result.ShardID="shard-b1" and passes (ShardIDFromResultPath=="shard-b1"); shardIDPattern passes. Only line 419 rejects the mismatch. Delete lines 419-422 and shard-3a is recorded as covered by a result that names shard-b1, with no test failing. The completeness/coverage claim (ShardsCovered) is thus silently corruptible and unguarded by the suite.
tests_checked: TestRenderersNeutraliseShardIDAndVerdict (sets ShardID="mrvf-injected-shard" but only asserts no "mrvf-" token survives rendering, not the blocker); TestAggregateValidatesResultFieldShape/"bad shard id" (asserts "invalid shard ID" from line 479, passes with or without 419); TestFilenameIdMismatchBlocks (mutates Path, keeps ShardID="shard-3a"); no test asserts the "declares shard" blocker.

issue_text: validRationale returns false for len(value) < 12 at line 613, THEN switches on lowercased value rejecting "n/a", "none", "to"+"do" (="todo"), "tbd" at lines 616-621. All four literals are 3-4 characters, strictly less than 12, so the length guard already returns false before any of them can reach the switch. The switch's reject cases are unreachable dead code; the switch can be deleted with all tests passing.
why_real: Category 3 (guard that cannot fire). The switch's stated purpose is to reject placeholder rationales like tbd/todo/n/a/none, but the preceding `len(value) < 12` check subsumes every listed literal (max length 4). No input can trigger the switch's `return false`. The only test that exercises a placeholder (Rationale="tbd") is caught by the length check, not the switch, so the switch is both dead and untested.
tests_checked: TestAggregateRequiresCompletePathAccounting (sets Rationale="tbd", asserts "invalid disposition rationale" — satisfied by the len<12 branch); no test passes a >=12-char string equal to any switch case (impossible for these literals).

issue_text: severityBlocks (line 646) excludes SeverityLow from the blocking set, so a low-severity finding with an open/waived/deferred disposition does not block a PASS. No test pins this exclusion: every test that uses SeverityLow pairs it with another blocker (unknown disposition, missing evidence) or a closing disposition. severityBlocks could be changed to treat low as blocking (e.g. `value != ""`) and the entire suite still passes.
why_real: Category 2 (invariant invertible with tests still passing). The intended behavior 'a low-severity open finding does not block' is unverified. Verified by walking each SeverityLow test: TestAggregateValidatesResultFieldShape/"unknown disposition" (Disposition "shrug" fails validFindingDisposition, else-branch skipped), /"finding evidence" (Disposition Fixed closes via dispositionCloses so severityBlocks result is irrelevant, plus separate evidence blocker). passingShardResult carries no findings, so no passing manifest contains a bare Low+Open finding.
tests_checked: TestWaivedMediumFindingBlocks (uses SeverityMedium only); TestFixedAndFalsePositiveClose (SeverityCritical + closing disposition); TestAggregateValidatesResultFieldShape/"unknown severity","unknown disposition","finding evidence" (Low always accompanied by another blocker or closing disposition). None asserts a Low finding is non-blocking.
